title: label prioritization signal playground
content:
Notes to self - label prioritization / signal playground

Purpose:
- sketch cheap rules & sampling heuristics to prioritize which items go to fast auto-clean vs. full manual adjudication.
- keep small, actionable examples we can hand off to on-call labelers or use to seed a sampler.

Background/context:
- volume spikes ~ weekly from web scrape + partner batch. We have limited adjudication (~200/hr) so need to route the long-tail to cheaper lanes.
- downstream quality SLO: 98% exact-label agreement on top-traffic flows; acceptable degradation (95%) on low-frequency classes.

High-level lanes (draft):
1) fast-pass auto-normalize (rules + high-confidence model):
   - trivial dedupe, simple regex normalization, currency canonicalization, phone-format unify.
   - only apply when model_confidence >= 0.95 AND metadata.token_count <= 24
   - reject if contains ambiguous markers (see below)
2) human light-touch (micro-edit):
   - single-label corrections, low-ambiguity category mapping; 1-label change expected
   - route if model_confidence in [0.7, 0.95) or if rule triggers with low conflict score
3) full adjudication queue (pair review + adjudicator):
   - multi-entity conflicts, swapped spans, nested entities, longfree-text contexts (>200 tokens)
4) privacy/blocker review:
   - PII, legal hold markers, or customer-reported content => immediate manual review

Signals we should prototype (cheap, interpretable):
- model_confidence (float) from ensemble; threshold tuning per label family
- metadata.correlation_count: how often same sample seen across batches (duplication -> safe auto-clean)
- token_entropy: normalized token-level perplexity indicator (high -> more ambiguity)
- presence_of_urls_or_ids: binary; urls with path params -> higher manual priority
- punctuation_density: heuristic for OCR/noisy scraped text (many odd punctuation => manual)
- competitor-entity-hit: fuzzy match to known brand list (if true -> escalate)

Corner / edge cases (examples + quick rule notes):
- "US 12345" - is this a zip or product code? If metadata.locale==US and 5-digit purely numeric -> treat as postcode, else keep as free token.
- "A/B test" - slash often tokenized as separate; if label is TASK or ACRONYM, map slash-preserve. Rule: preserve slashes for uppercase tokens >1 char.
- phone-like sequences inside long free text: if leading "+" or parentheses -> likely phone -> PII lane.
- combined currency+qty: "$5k" -> normalize to USD and expand to 5000 if unit marker 'k' present. But flag when text ambiguous like "5k views" -> not currency. Use adjacency heuristics: currency_symbol present OR preceding token currency_word in {USD, dollars}.

Quick sampling heuristics to surface high-impact items for manual review:
- stratify by frequency decile (bottom 10% frequency) + model_confidence < 0.8 AND (token_entropy > 0.6 OR punctuation_density > 0.2)
- prioritize items with high negative feedback (customer flags) irrespective of confidence
- sample boundary cases where two top labels differ by <0.05 confidence for human check (we see many boundary flips)

Adjudicator tiebreaker cheat sheet (for humans):
- prefer canonical product names over local nicknames unless explicit brand token present
- when in doubt about span boundaries, prefer smaller span that preserves a complete token (avoid chopping hyphenated words unless hyphen meant to separate two concepts)
- timestamps: prefer ISO-ish normalized form if context suggests machine-readable (e.g., '2024-08-12'), else keep original text if ambiguous shorthand like '8/12' and locale unknown

Mini examples (for sampler):
- "chargeback-ID: 001-AB/23" -> route to manual, slash + alpha-numeric + 'ID' marker
- "Sold 5k units for $2 each" -> auto-normalize quantity but flag '5k' ambiguity; safe if currency_symbol present and following token 'each'
- "Acme corp. vs. ACME" -> case-sensitive brand collision; escalate to adjudication; prefer uppercase full brand if legal mention exists.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- How useful is token_entropy as computed from our distil ensemble for routing? Pilot: 10k sample, bucket by entropy, measure manual-change-rate.
- Calibration of model_confidence across label families: per-label thresholds likely much better than global.
- Explore cheap regex-explainability scoring for auto-clean filters - does adding rule-explain increase trust for labelers? Quick user study planned.

To-do (next week):
- implement a lightweight router prototype that uses three signals: model_confidence, token_entropy, presence_of_urls_or_ids.
- produce a 500-item sample from bottom frequency decile + low-confidence for human review and measure triage time per item.
- write up 1-pager for labeling team with lane definitions and 6 annotated examples.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally messy. The goal is a runnable list of heuristics we can iterate on with Marco and Jade. When we land a stable rule, move to confluence and add a unit test for sampler.

Scratch regexes/triggers (very rough):
- phone-ish: "(\\+?\\d{1,3}[\\s-])?(\\(\\d{3}\\)|\\d{3})[\\s-]?\\d{3}[\\s-]?\\d{4}"
- zip-us: "^\\d{5}(-\\d{4})?$"
- currency: "(^|\\W)(\\$|USD|usd|dollars?)\\s?\\d{1,3}(,\\d{3})*(\\.\\d+)?"

Last thought: prioritize fast-payoff heuristics first (currency, phone, urls, excessive punctuation). Those reduce 30-40% of trivial manual cost in other projects. If we can demonstrate 15% adjudication-hours reduction in 2 sprints, we can push for a small routing feature in the labeling UI.

End of scratchpad.
